3.5-1. COMPETITIVE RESPONSE SIMULATION  **score: −1**

  • Off-price (TJX/ROSS/Burlington) does not counter-move; it has

    response is passive and structurally negative.
  • Amazon's response to a beauty/apparel recovery is a pricing and
    private-label response, not a store response — it costs Amazon
    little and costs Macy's margin. This is the most likely counter.
  • Department-store peers (Kohl's, JCPenney, Belk) are weaker and
    will discount into any Macy's share gain, particularly in the
    middle-income segment where Macy's namesake competes. Risk of a
    price war in the value tier that contaminates the Backstage
    off-price layer.
  • Bloomingdale's is the least contestable asset: Saks Fifth Avenue
    and Neiman Marcus (post-merger) are the only direct peers and
    both are financially constrained. This is where the competitive
    response is weakest — supporting the mix-shift thesis.
  NET: the response is mild on the luxury end and adverse in the
  middle, i.e. it reinforces the mix shift rather than reversing it,
  and it argues against a terminal margin above ~8.5%.

3.5-3. CUSTOMER BEHAVIOUR EVOLUTION
